rows.text_1_facilitator::eng: Today’s skill is all about how to help your child follow instructions. 😃
rows.text_2::eng:
Even the best behaved children only follow instructions about 50% of the time. ⏰

Being more effective about how you give instructions can make things more peaceful and calm at home. 🌱

rows.text_1_facilitator::eng: What do you think about this?
rows.quiz_1_question::eng: True or false: It does not matter whether you give an instruction in a positive or negative way.
rows.quiz_1_feedback_1::eng:
❌ That’s incorrect. 

Children are more likely to follow an instruction when it is worded in a positive way. 

💙 Negative instructions like, “Don’t do that!” can make children (and us) feel bad 😣
rows.quiz_1_feedback_2::eng:

rows.text_1_facilitator::eng: 3️⃣ Here are three tips on how to help your child follow instructions more often:
rows.section_1_text::eng:
⭐Say the behaviour you want your child to do. For example: “Please take your shoes off when you come inside, Adam.”
👀Use your child’s name to get their attention, go down to their level, and make eye contact.
rows.section_2_text::eng:
⭐Give instructions your child can follow. 
💡 Give one instruction at a time - it is easier to remember.
⏰ Try giving a heads-up: “In 3 minutes, it will be bedtime and you will need to give the handphone back to me.”
rows.section_3_text::eng:
⭐Use positive words when giving instructions. For example, say “Talk in a quiet voice,” instead of “Don’t shout.”
💡Speak calmly but firmly, like you expect your child to do what you ask.
🎁 Praise, praise, praise! Make sure you praise your child immediately when they follow your instruction.
🌷And remember—this takes practice. Be kind to yourself as you learn too. 💙

rows.quiz_1_question::eng: Your home activity for today is to try to give specific, realistic, and positive instructions with your child. Do you have time to do this today? ⏰⭐
rows.quiz_1_feedback_1::eng: 🎉That's great! Try to remember to praise your child whenever they follow your instruction. You can do it!
rows.quiz_1_feedback_2::eng: 💚That's OK! Learning something new takes time, patience, and practice. You might want to start by thinking of 1 instruction that you find yourself giving your child a lot of the time. Practice with your partner first! 🔄
